newsitem.title: USA: Warner changes ads with doctored photo of opponent.
newsitem.headline: Warner changes ads with doctored photo of opponent.

text.p: Facing a hail of criticism, Virginia Sen. John Warner Thursday hurriedly removed a doctored picture of his Democratic opponent from a television advertisement airing around the state.

The Republican senator came under fire earlier this week when it was discovered his campaign was running an ad that included a picture with his opponent's head superimposed on the body of Virginia's Democratic Sen. Chuck Robb.

The altered picture made it appear challenger Mark Warner was shaking hands with Virginia's former Democratic Gov. Douglas Wilder as a smiling President Clinton looked on. It was part of a negative ad accusing Mark Warner, a businessman and former chairman of the state Democratic party, of being a liberal political insider.

"What John Warner and his campaign did was an outrage and a gross disservice to the people of Virginia," the Democrat said in a statement. "No political talk can cover up the fact that this was a blatant attempt to deceive the people of Virginia. It may be new technology but it's the worst of old-style politics."
Mark Warner has supported Clinton and Wilder and did attend the event in the offending picture.

Republican aides said the doctored photo had been removed from most of the ads Wednesday evening. The ad was also notable because it was one of the first times John Warner, running well ahead in polls, had used negative attacks.

His campaign blamed media consultant Greg Stevens, who produced the ad. Stevens issued a statement apologising for it Thursday, saying the decision to alter the photograph was the result of orders from Warner not to show Robb in commercials.

On Thursday, a new Virginia Commonwealth University poll was released showing that Sen. Warner led his Democratic challenger by 16 points. Clinton also leads Republican challenger Bob Dole in the state by 7 percentage points. The poll, conducted Oct 2-11, has a four percentage point margin of error.
